needs_you_intro: These are questions about what you offer, so only you can answer them. I changed none of this wording.

needs_you.title: The yearly plan is paid upfront, and the terms do not say what happens if a restaurant stops
needs_you.detail: Today's change added "$2,700 per year paid upfront, cancel anytime on the monthly plan". A restaurant that pays for the year and leaves in month four will ask whether it gets money back. The terms are silent, and "cancel anytime" now applies to the monthly plan only.
needs_you.action: Decide the rule, for example no refund, or a refund of the unused months, and tell me. I will add one sentence.

needs_you.title: The homepage still says "One flat price" and "no 12-month contract"
needs_you.detail: The fine print under the claim form now reads "$250/mo, or $2,700 a year" and, one line below, "One flat price. No per-cover fees, no paying per click, no 12-month contract." Both are defensible, since the yearly plan is a choice. A careful owner may still read two prices next to "one flat price" as a contradiction. The questions section I added repeats the same wording.
needs_you.action: Tell me if you want different words, for example "No per-cover fees, no paying per click, no contract you cannot leave".

needs_you.title: The founding rate is not written anywhere on the site
needs_you.detail: Your commit messages today mention a founding rate of $149 a month for the first 10 pilot restaurants. The site and these terms only state $250. If pilot restaurants are told $149, the terms they can read say something else.
needs_you.action: Either add the founding rate to the terms, or keep it as a private offer and accept that the public terms show the standard price. Your call.
needs_you.effort: 5 minutes if you want it added

needs_you.title: Before you charge anyone, have the terms checked
needs_you.detail: The terms are clear and honest. They do not yet say who the contract is with, which law applies, or what Rihla is and is not liable for, and they do not mention Members Area accounts. That was fine for a free pilot. It matters once money changes hands.
needs_you.action: A short review by a lawyer. I can then put the result into the same plain style.

changes_intro: Everything below is committed on `claude/practical-keller-adcqrc`. The page looks the same apart from the date and one new line.

changes.title: "Last updated" now matches the last change
changes.why: The section "Changes to these terms" says the date at the top shows the latest version. The paid tier changed from $79 to $250 with a yearly option on November 11, and the date still said November 2. It is corrected, and wrapped in a `<time>` tag so machines can read it. If you publish on a later day, set it to that day.

changes.title: New line: where the data rules are
changes.why: The terms and the Privacy Policy did not refer to each other. A reader of the terms now finds the policy in one click, and search engines get a link between the two pages. It is a pointer, not a new term.

Your data

changes.title: Each section can be linked to

changes.title: Same font request as the homepage
changes.why: The page now sends the identical request, so a visitor arriving from the homepage already has it cached.

changes.title: Taller tap areas in the footer
changes.why: The footer links were 17 px tall. They are now 29 px to tap, and the footer is the same height as before.

changes.title: Sitemap date
changes.why: The entry for this page in `sitemap.xml` now says it changed today.

changes.title: Google Analytics and the cookie notice
changes.why: The page now carries the homepage's tag and loads `site.js`. A visit to the terms is counted, and a visitor who lands here first is asked about cookies.

changes.title: `cta_click` on 5 links
changes.why: `terms_contact_email` shows how often the terms lead to a question by email. `terms_privacy` shows whether anyone follows the new link.
